tonight.headline: No claim tonight; two receivers go back in, conditionally
body: Bad news first. You are 0–4, and the two receivers ESPN put back into your projection lineup today, Jefferson and McLaurin, came back on a label and not on a report: neither has practised since he was hurt and neither coach has said he will play. As set you project 115.1 against 117.5 and ESPN gives you 49%.

Waivers process tonight at 01:00 Mexico City and this is the last brief before they do. My answer is no claim. Then set Jefferson for Addison and McLaurin for Kamara, with each benched man as the fallback, and read Wednesday's practice reports.

case.label: Their side
case.body: Ja'Marr Chase, their top projection at 21.9, is in the concussion protocol: 'day-to-day', re-evaluated Wednesday (Zac Taylor, 5 Oct). Chuba Hubbard is still in their flex on a bye at 0.0, so their 117.5 rises when they fix it. McBride 18.8, Purdy 18.0, London 16.0, Irving 15.3.

case.label: Your side
case.body: As set: Allen 20.1, Warren 14.6, Wilson 14.6, Tuten 14.0, Likely 12.9, Addison 11.4, Kamara 11.2, Fairbairn 8.5, the Vikings 7.8. The projection lineup is 124.3, which is 9.2 higher, and all 9.2 depends on two men being active.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Jefferson or McLaurin missing practice through Friday, on your side. Chase being ruled out, on theirs.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Both kick off Sun 11:00 Mexico City · check inactives 09:30
doFirst.title: Jefferson back in for Addison, if he is active
doFirst.subtitle: 18.6 against 11.4. ESPN changed his label from OUT to QUESTIONABLE today; his coach has not changed his answer. Addison is the fallback.

case.label: What the check says
case.body: As set you project 115.1; the projection lineup is 124.3. Of that 9.2, Jefferson over Addison is 7.2, which the lineup check labels PROJECTION and not a coin flip.

case.label: What is and isn't known
case.body: He sprained an ankle on 27 Sep, missed Week 4 and did not practise last week. Kevin O'Connell on Monday: 'We'll see how he does throughout the week. I don't have any real projection on whether we'll have him or not.' He also mentioned the Week 6 bye, which Pro Football Network reads as a reason they might rest him. Heavy writes that he is 'expected to return'; that is its wording, not the coach's. Nothing was reported on Tuesday, and I could not load ESPN's own note on the change.

case.label: Why set it now
case.body: Because both men play in the same game at 11:00 on Sunday, so nothing locks early and the fallback costs nothing. Setting it today means a missed check leaves 18.6 in the slot if he plays. The risk runs the other way: if he is inactive and you don't look at 09:30, the slot scores zero.

case.label: The dates that matter
case.body: Practice reports on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday. No practice by Friday means Addison keeps the slot. Thursday's brief reads the first two.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Jefferson is active and Addison outscores him on Sunday (archive). If he is inactive the card never fires and Addison starts.

doFirst.sources: lineup_check.py · Heavy · Pro Football Network · Audacy/WCCO · Yahoo

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Both kick off Sun 11:00 Mexico City · check inactives 09:30
doFirst.title: Flex: McLaurin over Kamara, if he is active
doFirst.subtitle: 13.2 against 11.2, which the lineup check files as a coin flip. It goes to the projection, with Kamara as the fallback.

case.label: What the check says
case.body: The other 2.0 of the 9.2. Inside two points ESPN is right 56% of the time, so this gets no thesis and nothing in the decision log.

case.label: What is and isn't known
case.body: McLaurin hurt a hamstring in practice on Fri 2 Oct and was inactive in London. Dan Quinn on Monday: 'We're still evaluating. I'll give you a better update for him for Wednesday.' Jayden Daniels is expected to practise in full and start, which is an upgrade on the quarterbacks McLaurin missed.

case.label: This morning's flex card is withdrawn
case.body: The morning brief put Gordon in the flex over Kamara, 11.0 to 10.0. ESPN now has Kamara at 11.2 and Gordon at 10.9, with nothing reported in between. You left Kamara there, which the afternoon numbers agree with. Kamara's knee scare on Monday still has no update.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: McLaurin is active and Kamara outscores him on Sunday (archive). On a coin flip that happens almost half the time.

whatWentWrong.title: Tonight's waiver run passes with no claim, and that is the recommendation
whatWentWrong.lead: Claims process at 01:00 Mexico City on Wednesday, before any of your three hurt receivers practises. You are first in the order and the claim would succeed. It still isn't worth a seat.

case.label: The evidence
case.body: The only claim with a case is DK Metcalf: 12.1 this week, targets 10, 9, 5, 9. Every seat he could take is closed. Coker is expected back for Week 6 and ESPN's season number has him at 180.4 to Metcalf's 153.8. Addison was added on 1 Oct, inside the seven-day churn window until Thursday, and he is Jefferson's fallback in the first card. Monangai and Gordon have open holds; Kamara and Gordon are protected while Etienne and Achane are out.

case.label: What it changes
case.body: Nothing in the lineup: both cards above use players you already own. It does mean Thursday is the day to look again. If Jefferson practises, Addison stops being needed as a fallback, his seat is seven days old, and Metcalf is a free agent if nobody claims him tonight. He was dropped on 30 Sep and went unclaimed last week.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Before 01:00: Coker going on injured reserve or being reported out past Week 6. Either makes Metcalf for Coker a claim worth making tonight. I found neither.

whatWentWrong.sources: ESPN league file · activity log · Yahoo · RotoWire

whatWentWrong.title: ESPN's labels moved today and the reporting didn't
whatWentWrong.lead: This morning Jefferson and McLaurin were OUT and the lineup check left them out. This afternoon they are QUESTIONABLE and it starts both.

case.label: The evidence
case.body: Neither research pass found a report dated Tuesday on either player. The newest facts are Monday's press conferences, which this morning's brief already had. ESPN's own pages returned nothing, so the reason is my inference: a Week 4 OUT tag being cleared for the new week.

case.label: What it changes
case.body: Both cards. The projection lineup is the rule, so they go in; the contingency is the protection, so each has a named fallback and a time to check. The 9.2-point gap the check reports is the size of the bet, not a measure of how far the lineup is from right.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Wednesday's practice reports. A limited session for either is the first real evidence since the injuries.

worthALook.name: DK Metcalf
worthALook.lead: Carried from this morning, re-checked: still the receiver to add, still not tonight. Thursday is the day.

case.label: The role
case.body: 5 catches on 9 targets for 115 on Thursday, 16.5 (archive); targets 10, 9, 5, 9. 97% of the snaps and 87% of the routes in Week 4 (RotoWire). No injury. His first three games were 11 catches for 98 yards, so it is one efficient game on steady volume.

case.label: The number that kills it tonight
case.body: The seat. Coker's is the only one without a rule on it and ESPN's season number has him at 180.4 to Metcalf's 153.8, with a Week 6 return expected. Addison's seat opens on Thursday, when it is seven days old.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Thursday, as a free agent, for Addison, if Jefferson has practised and Metcalf went unclaimed tonight. Tonight only if Coker goes on injured reserve before 01:00.

worthALook.sources: Week 1–4 archive · RotoWire · The Fantasy Footballers · ESPN league file

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Targets 4, 7, 4, 7 against Metcalf's 10, 9, 5, 9; it is deep-ball efficiency, and KC Concepcion led Cleveland with 8 targets and a 100% route share. You dropped Boston on 1 Oct.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Not this week. Second choice behind Metcalf, and only if Metcalf is claimed tonight.

worthALook.name: Rico Dowdle
worthALook.lead: Carried: the back who takes carries from your Warren when he returns, and that may be Sunday.

case.label: The role

With him active Warren took 56% and 55% of the carries; without him, all of them (archive). ESPN moved him from OUT to QUESTIONABLE today.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: A handcuff to a back you start, on a roster with five backs and no free seat. He ran 15 times for 37 yards before the injury.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Nothing makes him an add here. His practice status on Wednesday matters for Warren's number, not for your roster.

doNotChase.name: Joe Mixon
doNotChase.lead: Still the wire's biggest riser, and the reason is gone: Seattle did not sign him.

case.label: The rise
case.body: Monday's reports had him joining Seattle's practice squad. Monday's waiver columns still say so.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: On Tuesday Seattle 'opted against signing' him after his physical (Schefter via NFL.com; FantasyPros, 6 Oct, 14:07 ET). He has no team, missed all of 2025 with a foot injury and has no projection.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: A signing to a 53-man roster and a coach describing a role.

doNotChase.lead: Every column's top pickup this week, and ESPN now projects him 10.3. A sixth back for you.

case.label: The rise
case.body: Tank Bigsby had core-muscle surgery and is on injured reserve, and Saquon Barkley is 'likely out' for London (Philadelphia Inquirer, 6 Oct), so Shipley is the only healthy back on the roster. RotoWire's column puts its biggest bid on him.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: 6 carries for 23 on 47% of the snaps: 2.3 (archive); 15 carries all season. 10.3 is below all five of your backs, the Inquirer names three practice-squad backs who may be elevated, and Jacksonville allow the second-fewest standard points to running backs.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Barkley ruled out for a month, and one of your backs ruled out with him.

doNotChase.sources: Philadelphia Inquirer · RotoWire · Yahoo · Week 4 archive · FootballDB

doNotChase.name: Tyreek Hill
doNotChase.lead: Carried: closer to a team than he was, and still without one.

case.label: The rise
case.body: Tyquan Thornton is out 12 to 16 weeks after ankle surgery and Kansas City have contacted Hill's agent. Drew Rosenhaus on Monday: 'I would anticipate Tyreek potentially signing with a team over the next few days.'

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: No signing as of Tuesday afternoon. He is coming back from a dislocated knee with torn ligaments and is 'at least a month away from potentially playing' (Yahoo, 6 Oct). Two of your bench seats already hold receivers who may not play this week.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: A signing, then a practice.

doNotChase.name: Tucker Kraft
doNotChase.lead: Carried: an 85%-owned tight end on your wire, at a position with one slot and Likely in it.

case.label: The rise
case.body: 6 catches on 7 targets for 42 and his first touchdown, a season high in catches as he comes back from last season's ACL tear (FantasyPros, 5 Oct).

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: 10.5 against Likely's 12.9, and Chem's flex takes only backs and receivers. A second tight end has no way into this lineup.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Likely on a Giants injury report.

doNotChase.sources: FantasyPros · CBS Sports · ESPN league file

doNotChase.name: Cowboys D/ST
doNotChase.lead: New this afternoon: the highest-projected free defence, 0.9 above yours, against an undrafted rookie quarterback.

case.label: The rise
case.body: Dallas host Tampa Bay on Thursday. Baker Mayfield has a dislocated thumb and Jalon Daniels, who threw two interceptions in his first start, plays again. PFN and DraftSharks both rank Dallas 6th for the week.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: 8.7 against the Vikings' 7.8. Under a point isn't a streaming move, the same two lists rank Minnesota 4th and 1st, and a claim tonight would need a seat.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Nothing this week. Next Tuesday you need a defence for Minnesota's bye, and Dallas play at Green Bay in Week 6.

doNotChase.sources: ESPN league file · PFN · DraftSharks · CBS Sports

doNotChase.name: Malik Washington
doNotChase.lead: Carried: Yahoo's receiver add of the week, in an offence that threw for 85 yards.

case.label: The rise
case.body: 5 catches on 5 targets for 67, 12.0 (archive); target shares of 28% and 29% in the last two weeks and 86% of the snaps in three of four games (Yahoo, 5 Oct).

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Targets 8, 5, 10, 5 from Malik Willis, who was 9 of 17 for 85. Miami are off in Week 6, the same week as your Vikings.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Eight or more targets against Cincinnati, or a different quarterback in Miami.

doNotChase.name: Makai Lemon
doNotChase.lead: Carried: six targets with Smith out, in an offence that threw for 93 yards.

case.label: The rise
case.body: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) is expected to miss multiple games (Inquirer, 5–6 Oct). Lemon played 45 of 61 snaps.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: 3 catches on 6 targets for 27, 5.7 (archive), and no more than 30 yards in any game. Darius Cooper played 55 snaps and caught both touchdowns.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Eight or more targets in London.

doNotChase.sources: Week 4 archive · NBC Sports Philadelphia · Philadelphia Inquirer · CBS Sports

waiverAnalysis.summary: The same four receivers clear the tool's bar as this morning, and the bar is still partly an artefact: it measures them against Coker, whose last two weeks are an injury and a missed game. Four weeks of data. None has a role reason strong enough to act on, and nothing clears at running back or tight end.

rising.name: Romeo Doubs
rising.roleReason: 6 catches on 9 targets with two touchdowns against Buffalo, his first big game, after Mack Hollins left with a calf injury. A.J. Brown, now a Patriot, is on injured reserve with a high-ankle sprain and eligible to return in Week 6; Pelissero says he is 'pushing hard to be back ASAP'.
rising.action: WATCH — one nine-target game, with the team's best receiver eligible to return in a week

rising.name: Dohnte Meyers
rising.roleReason: 7 catches on 9 targets after Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor) left, with Joe Burrow throwing 54 times. Both are day-to-day and neither is ruled out (Zac Taylor, 5 Oct). Cincinnati are off in Week 6.
rising.action: WATCH — the role exists only if Chase and Higgins both sit

rising.name: Khalil Shakir
rising.roleReason: 7 catches on 8 targets for 82, a season best, in the game DJ Moore left with an aggravated AC-joint sprain. Moore's status is open and 'not long term' (Schefter); Keon Coleman, 6 for 116 and a touchdown, is the Bill the columns prefer.
rising.action: WATCH — depends on Moore missing Monday night, and Coleman is ahead of him for the extra targets

rising.name: KC Concepcion
rising.roleReason: The steadiest of the four: a team-high 8 targets and 37 routes in Week 4, a 100% route share, and 17 targets in two weeks (RotoWire; NFL.com). The Browns said they want Watson to get him more involved. The volume is real and the production isn't yet: 7.6 a game.
rising.action: WATCH — a real role at 7.6 points a game; behind Metcalf if a seat opens on Thursday
rising.sources: RotoWire · NFL.com · NBC Sports · Week 1–4 archive

Star Tribune, Hogs Haven, Bleeding Green Nation, Stampede Blue, Arrowhead Pride, Field Gulls and Pro Football Rumors were blocked; RotoBaller and several NBC Sports pages gave no article body; FantasyPros' tables did not render. Pages were read through a summarising tool, so quotes are close but may not be exact.
